description.narrative:
Project Outcome Stakeholders access to finance for SMEs including women-owned SMEs: While Chile has made progress in reducing the gender gap in terms of financial access, a significant gender disparity still exists especially in access to credit, as only 23% of the systems commercial loans are destined to women-owned enterprises. The financing provided by IFC will help Tanner to execute the goals established through its new sustainability framework created a in 2023 which includes goals to increase its financing to sustainable areas such as women-owned businesses and clean transportation.
Stakeholder effects Access to climate finance, electric vehicle financing: Financial institutions like Tanner will play a critical role to support the transition to a cleaner way of transportation . Through the Project, IFC will support Tanner to help the Company develop a strategy to further strengthen its lending operations in electromobility.
Market Creation Sustainability: One of the mayor contributors to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in Chile is the transportation sector. In order to achieve a de-carbonization of the transportation sector, Chile will require a fast uptake of electric vehicles (EVs). In this project, IFC will support Tanner in transforming into a commercial bank, bringing in a new player in the segment with a clear strategy focused on clean transportation. IFC anticipates that the Project will show other players the financial viability and growing opportunities in EV financing, supporting green transportation, and leading to the reduction of GHG emissions through the demonstration and replication channels.

The proposed investment consists of: (i) an equity investment of up to US$20 million equivalent in Chilean pesos (CLP) in newly issued common shares of Tanner Servicios Financieros S.A. (Tanner or the Company) to support the Companys growth during the setup of a full commercial bank, and (ii) a 5-year senior unsecured convertible loan for up to US$20 million (the C Loan) to finance the Company and new banks electro mobility sub-projects and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) portfolio, including women-owned small and medium enterprises (WSMEs) (the Project). In January 2024, Tanner obtained a provisional authorization from the regulator to establish a banking subsidiary, the first of a 3-stage phased approval process. IFC will support the Company with capital to facilitate the transformation process.
